title: Eventual Consistency
explain: Eventual consistency promises one thing: if writes stop, all replicas converge to the same value. It says nothing about when, or about what a reader sees in the meantime. A write is acknowledged by one replica and spreads to the others in the background.
model:
My picture is news spreading through a town: everyone ends up knowing, but for a while two neighbours tell different stories.

```
write ─▶ replica 1 (ack)  ··· background ···▶ replica 2 ··▶ replica 3
read at replica 3 right now: old value   (converges later)
```

- **Anomalies to expect:** stale reads, reads that go backwards (replica 1 then a lagging replica 2), and your own write being invisible for a moment.
- **Session guarantees** fix the ones users notice: *read-your-writes* (route a user to the leader or a fresh replica right after they write) and *monotonic reads* (pin a session to one replica).
- **Convergence needs a conflict rule** for concurrent writes: last-write-wins (simple, silently drops one write), version vectors with a merge, or CRDTs. Background [repair](#/sd/f/leaderless-repair) and cache TTLs are what drive convergence.

**Use** for feeds, like counts, search indexes, caches ([cache invalidation](#/sd/f/cache-invalidation) is an eventual-consistency problem) and anything where a stale read is cheap. **Don't** for balances, unique usernames or the last item in stock: those need a [quorum](#/sd/f/quorum), a single leader or [consensus](#/sd/f/consensus). Choose per piece of data, not per system. See also [leader-based consistency](#/sd/f/leader-based-consistency).

details.q: What exactly does an eventually consistent store guarantee?
details.a: Only convergence: absent new writes, replicas eventually agree. No bound on how long, no guarantee about intermediate reads, no ordering across keys.

details.q: A user uploads a profile photo, is redirected, and sees the old one; seconds later it is fine. What guarantee was missing?
details.a: Read-your-writes. Fix by reading the user's own recent writes from the leader or a fresh replica, or by returning a version and requiring the replica to have reached it.

details.q: One leader and two followers, async with 300 ms lag; a client reads from a random node right after a write. What fraction is stale?
details.a: Two of three nodes (about 67%) are followers that have not applied the write yet, so roughly two thirds of such reads return the old value.
They need a conflict rule. LWW is simple but drops writes and trusts clocks; version vectors detect concurrency and keep both for merge; CRDTs merge automatically.
Replication streams, read repair, anti-entropy, hinted handoff, and cache TTLs or invalidations. Without active convergence, 'eventually' can mean never for cold data.
Feeds, like counts, search indexes, caches, analytics. Not balances, unique usernames or last-item inventory.

prompts.q: Explain eventual consistency to an interviewer and say how you would still give users read-your-writes.
points: No promise on when or what is seen meanwhile
Route recent writers to leader or fresh replica

prompts.q: Walk through the life of one write in an eventually consistent system.
points: Readers may see old value meanwhile

prompts.q: Decide which of feed, like count, balance, unique username and cache fit eventual consistency and why.
points: Feed, likes, cache: stale read is cheap
Balance and unique username need an arbiter
Use quorum, single leader or consensus for those
Decide per data type, not per system
